s1.syndrome_frame: chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with localized erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels with plump endothelial cells
positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34
key_facts: female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
lesions located on left upper arm, left axilla, and lateral thoracic region
lesions are firm, nonscaly, and have irregular borders
no triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma before lesion appearance
no fever, weight loss, or fatigue
histopathological examination shows thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels
endothelial cells are plump with no significant cytologic atypia
immunohistochemistry positive for CD31, CD34, and Ki-67 (<1%)
immunohistochemistry negative for podoplanin (D2-40) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches histopathological findings of irregularly branched blood vessels and positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34

shortlist.label: Tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with clinical presentation of slowly growing, erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: possible match given the presence of plump endothelial cells and positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and lack of significant cytologic atypia

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: remains a plausible diagnosis given the clinical and histopathological features, although less specific than other options

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders, along with the histopathological findings of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels and plump endothelial cells, is consistent with Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma. The immunohistochemistry results, including positivity for CD31 and CD34, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Tufted angioma
rejected.why: While tufted angioma can present with similar skin lesions, the histopathological findings in this case, such as the presence of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels, are more characteristic of Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
rejected.why: Epithelioid hemangioma typically presents with more distinct epithelioid endothelial cells and a different immunohistochemical profile, which does not match the findings in this case.

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Retiform hemangioendothelioma is characterized by a retiform pattern of blood vessels, which is not described in the histopathological examination of this case.

rejected.label: Hemangioma
rejected.why: Hemangioma is a more general term that encompasses various types of benign vascular tumors, but the specific histopathological and immunohistochemical features in this case are more consistent with Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
